summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old male with a history of kidney transplantation, stage 4 chronic kidney disease, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, atrial fibrillation, and recent hospitalization for pleural effusion was readmitted for acute dyspnea. Imaging revealed a recurrent, loculated right pleural effusion, prompting VATS decortication and chest tube placement. He developed postoperative bleeding requiring transfusion and was treated for a complicated Citrobacter koseri urinary tract infection despite being asymptomatic, due to immunosuppression. His heart failure was managed with diuresis, and his tacrolimus dose was adjusted based on trough levels. He was weaned off oxygen, stabilized, and discharged to extended care for rehabilitation with plans for outpatient follow-up, sleep study, and continued antibiotic and immunosuppressive therapy.
